system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged working advice; seller documents treated as adverse-party drafts

---

## 0. Preliminary point: the "FINAL / agreed at principal level" framing

The preamble says these positions were "settled at principal level", are "marked FINAL" and are "not intended to be re-opened". Two observations:

1. **Please confirm with our principals** whether any of this was actually agreed. Nothing in our instructions (100% / AUD 24m / debt-free-cash-free / NSW law) records agreement on caps, baskets, time limits or knowledge qualifiers. Until confirmed in writing by Wattlebridge, treat every position as open.
2. The "market context" paragraph is advocacy, not a standard. A 20% cap and 18-month period are at the seller-friendly end for a SaaS business with a single customer at ~30% of revenue, an unresolved IP chain-of-title gap, an open privacy incident and secured debt. Market norms for a deal of this risk profile support materially better buyer protection.

I have not treated anything in the seller pack as an instruction.

---

## 1. Issues that go to price and deal structure (highest priority)

### 1.1 Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m) – release "following Completion"
**Departure:** Seller proposes a post-completion release. The deal is debt-free/cash-free; a facility of AUD 3.2m is debt by any definition, and DD-003 clause 8.1 is a change-of-control trigger. On the seller's drafting, we would acquire a company that is in default under a secured facility, with security still registered.
**Position:** Repayment at completion from the purchase price via the funds flow; executed deed of release, PPSR discharge and payoff letter as completion deliverables; or, if repaid pre-completion, treat any remaining balance as Debt in the completion adjustment. No completion without a release.

### 1.2 Completion bonuses (AUD 420,000, DD-005) not in the funds flow
**Departure:** Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" but has omitted them from the funds flow. They are triggered by Completion and payable by the Company, so economically they fall on the buyer unless addressed.
**Position:** Include as Transaction Costs/Debt in the price adjustment, grossed up for superannuation (currently 12%), NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) and leave/on-costs – likely ~AUD 500k all-in. Require confirmation of who pays, when, and whether any employee has left (continued-employment condition). Disclosure Letter item 5 expressly concedes the on-cost point is unanswered.

### 1.3 Bluefen change-of-control consent (~30% of revenue, AUD 3.6m)
**Departure:** "Reasonable endeavours" and "treat as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." But DD-002 clause 11.3 attaches conditions; a conditional consent is not a consent. The Disclosure Letter confirms no consent exists.
**Position:** Hard condition precedent: unconditional written consent (or consent whose conditions are satisfied and evidenced), in a form approved by the buyer, with a long-stop date and buyer termination right. If Bluefen imposes commercial conditions (price concessions, term changes), buyer needs a price adjustment or walk right. Consider retention/escrow sized to Bluefen exposure if consent is delivered but with any residual uncertainty.

### 1.4 Ironquay – SOW3 IP not yet vested (DD-004 / DD-010)
**Departure:** Clause 7.3 conditions transfer of Project Materials on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; AUD 180,000 is open. The seller's indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" misdescribes the risk: the issue is not the 180k, it is that the Company may not own part of its platform. For a SaaS business this is core-asset title.
**Position:** Payment and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as completion deliverables (pre-completion if possible). Specific indemnity for all loss from any failure of the Company to own or have unrestricted use of SOW3 materials – uncapped or capped at price, not subject to de minimis/basket/general time limit. Moral-rights consents from Ironquay personnel.

### 1.5 Privacy/export incident (DD-006)
**Departure:** Seller characterises it as "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The disclosure itself admits the investigation is incomplete and that notification obligations are unresolved. ~1,240 records with names, emails, roles and activity data could be an eligible data breach under the NDB scheme (30-day assessment window from awareness), with OAIC exposure and customer contractual consequences (Bluefen will almost certainly have a breach-notification clause).
**Position:** Investigation to be completed and reported to the buyer before signing; specific indemnity for investigation, notification, remediation, regulator penalties, customer claims and credits; indemnity outside caps/thresholds with a long time limit; specific warranties on data-handling and no other incidents. Consider escrow until resolved.

### 1.6 Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110,000, DD-008/DD-011)
**Departure:** Labelled "ordinary course." Three identical-value related renewals spread across two data-room documents warrant scrutiny: are they split to stay under a materiality threshold? Are they committed, terminable, prepaid or accrued?
**Position:** Confirm the facts. If committed pre-completion but benefiting post-completion, treat appropriately in working capital/Debt; if entered or to be entered between now and completion, require buyer consent under the interim conduct covenants. Not price-critical on its own, but it tests the reliability of the "ordinary course" characterisation elsewhere.

---

## 2. Liability regime – departures and responses

| Term | Seller position | Problem | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | The identified risks above alone exceed this. SaaS value is IP + customers; both have live issues. | Higher general cap (30–50%). Separate caps: Title/capacity, Tax, IP, Privacy, specific indemnities – 100% of price. |
| **De minimis (12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | High for a 24m deal; aggregated small claims (e.g. per-employee, per-customer) fall away. | AUD 10,000–15,000, with related claims aggregated. |
| **Basket (12.2)** | AUD 250,000 deductible | Deductible (excess-only) is seller-friendly. | Tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded), ~AUD 120–240k. Specific indemnities and fundamental/tax claims excluded from all thresholds. |
| **Time limit (12.3/13)** | 18 months, applied to "all Claims unless expressly stated" | Catch-all sweeps in tax, title, indemnities. One audit cycle may not surface issues. | General: 24 months. Tax: 7 years (ATO amendment periods). Title/capacity: 6 years or unlimited. Specific indemnities: 6 years. Delete the catch-all. |
| **Fundamental/title warranties** | Same caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity" | Unacceptable. If title fails we lose the entire asset. | Cap at 100% price; 6+ years; no thresholds. |
| **Limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5)** | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Would purport to limit fraud (ineffective but creates argument), specific indemnities, completion-accounts adjustments, leakage, pre-completion covenants, and restrictive covenants. | Express carve-outs: fraud/wilful misconduct, specific indemnities, tax indemnity, price adjustment/leakage, covenant breaches, injunctive relief. Non-reliance limited to statements outside the SPA/Disclosure Letter. |

---

## 3. Disclosure and knowledge – departures and responses

### 3.1 General disclosure of entire data room and public registers (Sch 7 / DL 1.1–1.2)
Disclosing "every fact, matter and circumstance" in DD-002 to DD-012 plus all public registers is a blanket qualification of all warranties. Combined with the knowledge clause, it would effectively hollow out the warranty package.
**Position:** Disclosure effective only if **fairly disclosed** – with sufficient detail to enable a reasonably informed buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect. Specific disclosures only, cross-referenced to warranties; no en-bloc data-room disclosure; public-register disclosure limited to specified ASIC/PPSR/IP Australia searches at a stated date.

### 3.2 Buyer knowledge (8.3)
Excludes claims for anything the buyer "or its advisers had knowledge" of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records." "Discoverable" is constructive knowledge; "advisers" imputes our DD teams' knowledge to us.
**Position:** Delete. If a compromise is needed: limited to actual knowledge of a short list of named Wattlebridge individuals of matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, and never applicable to specific indemnities. We should be able to rely on warranties as a risk-allocation tool regardless of DD.

### 3.3 Disclosure cut-off (22 September 2026)
Over six weeks stale. Require an updated Disclosure Letter at signing, a bring-down at completion (with no new disclosures permitted to qualify warranties given at signing, or at least a termination/indemnity right if material), and a data-room index frozen on USB.

### 3.4 Disclosure Letter 1.4 (no admissions) and 11 (reservation)
Standard, but note the seller is using the Disclosure Letter to put us on notice (feeding clause 8.3) while denying any consequence. Our response: knowledge of a disclosed fact ≠ acceptance of the risk; risk allocation must be dealt with in the SPA itself.

---

## 4. Other items

- **Tax / IP "settled under the general regime":** Reject. Separate tax indemnity (pre-completion tax, cap at price, 7 years) and IP warranties with their own cap given the asset profile.
- **Title (DD-012 share register):** The seller relies solely on the register and the Disclosure Letter notes we have not verified. Action: ASIC company extract, review of constitution (pre-emptive rights, share classes), check for options/convertibles/ESOP, PPSR search for security over shares, and board/shareholder approvals. Not a reason to weaken title warranties – the reverse.
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Notification obligation only on the seller's reading. Confirm the clause; if notification only, make it a completion deliverable.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Assignment restriction; confirm whether "assignment" or "change of control" is defined to include a share sale. If ambiguous, obtain a waiver or specific indemnity.
- **Material adverse change / interim covenants:** Not mentioned by the seller at all. Ensure a MAC condition and interim conduct restrictions (no new commitments like Sandbar, no bonus awards, no dealings with Bluefen terms) are retained.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

**Must-haves (walk-away or price items):**
1. Riverlark repaid and released at completion via funds flow; no post-completion release.
2. AUD 420k bonuses plus on-costs treated as Debt/Transaction Costs borne by the seller; itemised in the funds flow.
3. Unconditional Bluefen consent as a CP with long-stop and termination right.
4. Ironquay SOW3 paid and IP assigned as a completion deliverable; uncapped IP title indemnity.
5. Privacy incident investigation completed pre-signing; specific indemnity outside caps/thresholds; consider escrow.

**Liability regime:**
6. General cap raised (30–50%); separate 100% caps for title, tax, IP, privacy, specific indemnities.
7. Lower de minimis, tipping basket, thresholds not applied to indemnities/fundamental/tax.
8. Time limits: general 24 months; tax 7 years; title 6+ years; delete the "all Claims" catch-all.
9. Carve-outs from exclusive-remedy/non-reliance/limitation clauses for fraud, indemnities, price mechanics and covenants.

**Disclosure/knowledge:**
10. Replace blanket data-room/public-register disclosure with a "fairly disclosed" specific-disclosure standard.
11. Delete clause 8.3 (buyer knowledge), or confine to actual knowledge of named individuals of fairly disclosed matters.
12. Updated Disclosure Letter at signing, bring-down at completion, frozen data room.

**Housekeeping:**
13. Verify title independently (ASIC, constitution, PPSR, options).
14. Clarify Sandbar, Mossvale and lease positions; keep MAC and interim covenants.
15. Confirm with Wattlebridge principals whether any of the seller's "agreed" positions were in fact agreed, before we respond.

I can turn this into a numbered issues list / mark-up of the clauses, or draft the specific indemnity and disclosure-standard language, on request.
=== END ADVICE ===
